lines.text: A hundred metres down, a bright red fish turns black.
Nothing happened to the fish. Water swallows red light first — and by a hundred metres, the red is completely gone.
So a red fish has no red light left to reflect. To anything looking at it, it's simply black.
And a hundred metres isn't deep. You're still in the sunlight zone. That runs to two hundred.
Now here's the strange part. Keep going down, and a lot of the animals you meet are red.
In a world with no red light at all — why would anything be red?
The answer is at level five. The whole dive is linked right here.
